text:
incident-bot: ALERT: tenant=acmehealth (dedicated-east-2) — sudden KV/prefix cache hit-rate collapse and rising p95. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.

Priya Sharma: got the page, jumping in. Seeing 5xx spikes and token latency up for acmehealth routing.

Mateo Ruiz: on it, I'm awake. Can someone paste the short query for KV cache telemetry?

Priya Sharma: use the quick query from metrics-bot: `kv_cache.hit_rate{tenant:acmehealth, pool:dedicated-east-2}` — current value 0.03 (normally ~0.72).

metrics-bot: kv_cache.hit_rate{tenant=acmehealth, pool=dedicated-east-2} = 0.031 (1m avg). kv_cache.evictions = +1200 in last 10m. p95_latency = 1420ms (baseline 320ms). errors.5xx.rate = 3.8% (baseline 0.1%).

Linh Tran: this looks like cache pollution — probably a noisy prefix authoring job from the customer or a batch request pattern bypassing prefixing. Any recent deploys to runtime?

EngRuntime: no runtime deploys in the last 6 hours. We do see a higher-than-usual influx of unique prefixes: `unique_prefixes{tenant=acmehealth}` jumped from ~2k to 85k in 8m.

Mateo Ruiz: ok next steps: (1) disable prefix/KV caching for acmehealth to stop pollution, (2) purge tenant-specific KV entries, (3) continue triage to identify root cause on customer side. I'll run the disable now and open a canary route fallback.

Priya Sharma: agree. Also prepare to isolate them to a new quarantine pool if disabling cache isn't enough.

Mateo Ruiz: running command:
```bash
# disable prefix caching for tenant
redwoodctl tenant update --id acmehealth --kv-cache.enabled=false --kv-cache.mode=prefixing
```

Mateo Ruiz: got `200 OK` from control plane. Applying config to dedicated-east-2. Pushing purge command next.

Mateo Ruiz: purge command:
```bash
redwoodctl kv purge --tenant acmehealth --prefix="acme_*" --confirm
```

metrics-bot: Action started: kv_purge(tenant=acmehealth, prefixes=acme_*). Estimated keys: ~120k.

Priya Sharma: heads up this purge may cause a short spike as requests fall back to cold model. Notify support/customer.

Karen Patel: drafting a quick customer message for acmehealth CX: "We're investigating increased latency and 5xx errors. We've temporarily disabled prefix caching on your dedicated pool and are purging cache entries to restore normal service. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Want to share before sending?

Mateo Ruiz: send that, add: "No model or code changes were made by Redwood in the last 6 hours; this is a cache/traffic pattern event."

Support Bot: Note created: INC-8421 — Customer notified, message sent to acmehealth CSM and eng liaison.

metrics-bot: After config change: kv_cache.hit_rate=0.05 -> purge started. p95 latency initial bump to 1.9s (expected), error rate trending down after 3 minutes.

Linh Tran: while purge continues, let's prepare isolation: create new temporary pool `quarantine-east-2-acme` and move acmehealth traffic there so other tenants unaffected.

EngRuntime: creating quarantine pool will take ~3-4m. Command: `infractl pool clone --source dedicated-east-2 --target quarantine-east-2-acme --tenant acmehealth --isolate=true`

infra-oncall: cloning pool now. Allocating reserved G4s. ETA 4m.

Mateo Ruiz: purge completed. metrics-bot showing kv_cache.hit_rate climbing to 0.71 in the quarantine pool once we started isolating keys.

metrics-bot: kv_cache.hit_rate{tenant=acmehealth, pool=quarantine-east-2-acme} = 0.72. p95_latency = 340ms. errors.5xx.rate = 0.12%.

Priya Sharma: that's good — looks like cache pollution was cross-tenant (shared pool) and we stopped bleed by isolating. Next: confirm whether customer's traffic pattern created high-cardinality prefixes — ask them for any batch jobs or changes.

Karen Patel: I've added a request to the customer-facing note: "Can you share any recent changes to prompt templating or bulk jobs that may generate many unique prefixes? If you need help identifying requests we can share sample request IDs." Sent to acmehealth eng liaison.

Mateo Ruiz: I'll keep prefixing disabled until customer confirms or we roll out a safer prefixing policy. Long term we should add tenant-level hard limits on unique prefixes and eviction policies that prefer not to thrash shared pools.

Linh Tran: agree — action items for postmortem: (A) throttle unique-prefix registration per tenant, (B) add per-tenant isolation triggers when unique_prefixes > threshold, (C) improve observability to show top offending prefixes and request fingerprints.

Priya Sharma: handoff time — infra-oncall will own overnight monitoring and customer comms while we prepare RCA. infra-oncall, you good to take it?

infra-oncall: taking handoff. Notes: cache disabled for acmehealth, purge done, traffic moved to quarantine-east-2-acme, p95 and 5xx back to baseline. I will monitor alerts and escalate if hit_rate drops or errors creep up.

Priya Sharma: thanks. Postmortem owner: Linh; timeline doc created in /incidents/postmortems/INC-8421. Assigning action owners: Mateo (temporary config + purge), Linh (RCA + infra changes), Karen (customer comms & follow-ups).

Support Bot: Reminder set: follow-up with acmehealth in 24h.

Mateo Ruiz: brief log snippet from runtime during the window (stripped):
```
[2025-03-16T03:22:11Z] tenant=acmehealth prefix=acme_order_9a8f3c id=... cache_miss
[2025-03-16T03:22:11Z] tenant=acmehealth prefix=acme_order_1b2c3d id=... cache_miss
... repeated thousands of unique prefixes within minutes
```

Priya Sharma: closing loop here — incident mitigated, customer notified, handoff done. Will reopen if metrics regress. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-8421 — KV/prefix cache pollution on tenant=acmehealth. Duration 38m. Postmortem assigned.
